proseChanges.summary: **Fixes — help articles no longer make conversations answer 500:** on v0.4.17 and v0.4.18, an installation with published help articles answered `500` when a member opened, or searched the inbox for, a conversation whose text overlaps an article, and on inbound mail that quotes one (the message was refused and no message was stored); a reply that quotes an article could not be saved either. Real D1 refuses the knowledge reference policy statement because, with every CTE reference expanded in place, it reaches about 100 FROM items. This release compiles the policy as one pipeline in which each relation is read once, with the same decisions: a copy needs one visible occurrence per reader, any other block its full source set, an author sees its own copy, no readers means nothing visible, and a statement that cannot be evaluated fails. Opening a restricted-article conversation now reads only the request's own readers and documents instead of every contact of the workspace (about 324,000 rows in a large imported workspace). Recording a generation's sources admits the blocks first, then records each source only while it stays visible, in two statements each within D1's limits. No data step is needed: deploy the new Worker. No migration. **Migrations:** No migrations since v0.4.18. v0.4.19 adds no migration file, so a v0.4.18 installation's migration ledger stays unchanged.
proseChanges.was: v0.4.18 is the last published release, with migrations through 321.
proseChanges.now: v0.4.19 includes the knowledge reference policy fix and adds no migration since v0.4.18. Published upgrade baselines are v0.4.18 and v0.4.17.
proseChanges.ownerAction: Update from v0.4.18 without resetting. Back up D1, R2, Durable Object state and private settings first. Use Node 22.20.0, pnpm 10.12.4 and pinned rer 0.2.105. Retain native owners, permissions, support history, files, erasure fences and every applied migration identity. v0.4.19 adds no migration, so a v0.4.18 installation applies nothing before the new Worker serves traffic. Earlier installations apply every missing published migration once, in filename order, BEFORE the new Worker serves traffic (v0.4.17 needs 321_legacy_import_files.sql, then `node scripts/legacy-import/upgrade.mjs --project <legacy project id>` once per workspace imported from legacy, as the v0.4.18 notes describe; v0.4.16 also needs 320_legacy_import_work_repair.sql); retain each migration's buyer steps. Run `rer deploy --dry-run` against the retained installation before any separately authorized deployment. No reset, cutover or production deployment is part of this release. Live-provider qualification and owner cutover remain separate.

pendingMigrations.buyerSteps: Back up D1 first; apply once after 321_legacy_import_files.sql, before serving the updated Worker. Additive only: creates two indexes on contacts (contacts_address_lookup on (project_id, lower(email)) and contacts_preferred_address_lookup on (project_id, lower(json_extract(metadata_json,'$.provided_email')))), so an inbound mail's contact lookups by address search an index instead of walking every contact of the workspace; no row changes and nothing is read, sent or queued. On a workspace of about 160,000 contacts it applies in under a second.

Back up D1 first; apply once after 322_contact_address_lookup.sql, before serving the updated Worker. Additive only: creates one index on knowledge_documents (knowledge_documents_version_url on (version_id, url)), so the knowledge reference policy's check that an older crawl version's page still has a current twin at the same URL searches an index instead of walking every page of the published version; no row changes and nothing is read, sent or queued. On a crawled site of a few thousand pages it applies in under a second.
